newsitem.title: USA: Hepatitis vaccine cuts liver cancer in children.
newsitem.headline: Hepatitis vaccine cuts liver cancer in children.

text.p: The rate of liver cancer among children has been cut in half in Taiwan, and a team of doctors says the credit goes to the country's program of vaccinating all children against the liver disease hepatitis B.

The team, led by Mei-Hwei Chang of National Taiwan University, reported in the New England Journal of Medicine to be published on Thursday that since a nationwide hepatitis B vaccination program was implemented in Taiwan in 1984, the liver cancer rate in children aged six to 14 declined to 36 per 10 million from 70 per 10 million between 1990 and 1994.

The findings also provide new evidence that the virus responsible for hepatitis B, which can damage or destroy parts of the liver and can, in severe cases, lead to cirrhosis or even death, is also responsible for liver cancer.
"These data are evidence that prevention of a viral infection in a population can reduce the incidence of a specific cancer," the researchers said.
Eighty-five countries, including the United States, now require infants to be immunized against hepatitis B.
